analysis:
## Analysis

### Existing files that need modification

**Lock primitives**
- `src/execution/lock.ts` (211 lines) — `acquireLock`, `releaseLock`, `tryExclusiveCreate` (module-private at line 38), `_lockDeps.rename` seam (line 20). The checkout lock's BUG-07/BUG-34 stale-reclaim race handling is the pattern the feature lock must mirror. `tryExclusiveCreate` must be exported so the feature lock reuses its `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` semantics and BUG-34 restore behavior instead of copying them. `acquireLock` currently returns `Promise<boolean>` and the record it writes (`{ pid, timestamp }` at line 170-173) must gain `host`; the result becomes a holder-carrying object so the error message can name the holding PID/host without a re-read race.
- `src/execution/helpers/index.ts` — re-exports `acquireLock`/`releaseLock`/`_lockDeps`; needs to gain `acquireFeatureLock`/`releaseFeatureLock`/`_featureLockDeps`.
- `src/execution/index.ts` — re-exports `acquireLock`/`releaseLock`/`_lockDeps`; needs to gain `acquireFeatureLock`/`releaseFeatureLock`/`_featureLockDeps`.

**Run lifecycle**
- `src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts` (423 lines) — single acquire site (`acquireLock` at the line `// Acquire lock to prevent concurrent execution`). The MEM-1 outer try/catch and the call to `initializeAfterLock` are the structure to extend. `_runSetupDeps` (line 62-67) gains `acquireLock` and `acquireFeatureLock` injection points. StatusWriter is constructed here (line 173-180) with `workdir` already in scope from `:142`, so this is the sole StatusWriterContext construction site.
- `src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-init.ts` — FIX-H16 inner catch at line 237 (releaseLock on init failure) is the second release site. Both release sites must release both locks in reverse order (feature first, checkout last).
- `src/execution/lifecycle/run-cleanup.ts` — `releaseLock(workdir)` at the bottom (always-release site). Must release feature lock before checkout lock.
- `src/execution/lifecycle/precheck-runner.ts` — `runPrecheckValidation` calls `runPrecheck` without a feature lock argument; must thread `featureLock: { outputDir, feature: ctx.featureName }` through (omitted when `ctx.featureName` is undefined).

**Precheck / tooling**
- `src/precheck/checks-config.ts` — `checkStaleLock(workdir: string): Promise<Check>` must accept an optional `featureLock?: { outputDir: string; feature: string }` and apply the new shared `isLockSuspect` predicate to both locks.
- `src/precheck/index.ts` — `PrecheckOptions` (lines 102-109) and `getEarlyEnvironmentBlockers(workdir)` (line 134) must accept and forward the optional `featureLock`; `_precheckDeps` (line 191) gains `checkStaleLock` alongside the existing `checkStorySizeGate`.
- `src/precheck/checks.ts` — re-export barrel; `checkStaleLock` is already exported through it.
- `src/commands/unlock.ts` (108 lines) — `unlockCommand({ dir?, force? })` must gain optional `feature`; with feature, resolves `<outputDir>/features/<feature>/nax.lock`; without one, runs the feature-lock scan (`features/*/nax.lock`) in addition to the checkout lock. `--force` overrides staleness for both kinds.
- `bin/nax.ts` (line 1355-1373) — `unlock` command registration must add `-f, --feature <name>` option and forward it.

**Project identity**
- `src/runtime/paths.ts` — `claimProjectIdentity` (line 75-101) currently throws `RUN_NAME_COLLISION` on any workdir mismatch. Must instead accept workdir mismatches when `isSameProject` holds, refreshing `lastSeen` and leaving stored `workdir` unchanged. `readProjectIdentity`/`writeProjectIdentity`/`projectOutputDir` are read-only symbols used as-is.
- `src/cli/init.ts` — `checkInitCollision` (line 69-79) has `sameRemote` (raw string equality) and `sameWorkdir` branches. Replace `sameRemote` with `isSameProject`, keep `sameWorkdir`.
- `src/commands/migrate.ts` — reads the same identity; no changes needed beyond ensuring the new identity record fields stay readable.
- `src/runtime/index.ts` (line 528+) — barrel; gains `isSameProject` re-export.

**Run identity / status**
- `src/execution/runner.ts` (line 176) — `run()` generates `run-${iso}` internally; options object gains optional `runId`.
- `src/commands/resume.ts` (line 191-201) — currently builds its own run ID at second resolution; must call `buildRunId` and pass it as `runId`.
- `src/execution/status-file.ts` — `NaxStatusFile.run` (line 105-127) gains optional `workdir`; `RunStateSnapshot` (line 255-273) gains optional `workdir`; `buildStatusSnapshot` (line 315-328) reads it.
- `src/execution/status-writer.ts` — `StatusWriterContext` (line 28-41) gains optional `workdir`.

**Errors**
- `src/errors.ts` (line 62) — `LockAcquisitionError(workdir)` must split into two distinguishable refusals (checkout vs feature) with holder data in context.

**Curator metrics reader**
- `src/plugins/builtin/curator/collect.ts:113` — `runs.find(r => r.runId === context.runId) ?? runs.at(-1)` positional fallback is the defect. Must fail-closed (return no observations + warn-log) when no entry matches.
- `src/plugins/builtin/curator/collect.ts:209` — feature+time-window guard at `:220-227` is the reference pattern, must not be regressed.

### Existing tests that need updating
- `test/unit/errors.test.ts` — asserts `LockAcquisitionError`'s message and exact-object context.
- `test/unit/execution/helpers.test.ts` — asserts `acquireLock` boolean result and record fields.
- `test/unit/utils/utils-helpers.test.ts` — four sites assert `acquireLock` boolean by identity.
- `test/unit/precheck/precheck-checks-tier1-blockers.test.ts` — five sites call `checkStaleLock(workdir)`; must add feature-lock cases.
- `test/unit/commands/unlock.test.ts` — asserts only the checkout lock; must cover feature lock and scan.

### Risks
- **Stale reclaim race (BUG-34)**: the feature lock's `acquireFeatureLock` MUST mirror the rename-then-verify-then-restore pattern from `src/execution/lock.ts:88-160` exactly. Without it, two processes reclaiming the same stale lock would both believe they hold it. The `tryExclusiveCreate` reuse is the key to safe restore.
- **Lock ordering deadlock**: spec requires fixed acquisition order (checkout → feature) and reverse release. A leaked feature lock is project-level and blocks every checkout until 2h.
- **Identity fingerprint regression**: workdir-based identity was the only `RUN_NAME_COLLISION` guard; relaxing it without the locking changes would let two processes mutate the same `~/.nax/<projectKey>/` tree.
- **Status-file schema**: `NaxStatusFile.run.workdir` is optional but readers (TUI, `nax status`) must tolerate its absence in pre-existing status.json files.
- **Precheck API drift**: `PrecheckOptions.featureLock` is optional, and the three `nax plan` call sites (`src/cli/plan-decompose.ts:246,269`, `src/cli/plan-runtime/index.ts:110`) plus `src/commands/precheck.ts:87-90` must continue working without it (checkout-only behavior).
- **No `mock.module()`**: `.nax/rules/forbidden-patterns-source.md:31` bans it, so injection points are mandatory; the seams are `_runSetupDeps.acquireLock`, `_runSetupDeps.acquireFeatureLock`, `_precheckDeps.checkStaleLock`, and `_featureLockDeps.featureLockPath`.

### Migration path / sequencing
The spec mandates that this feature lands AFTER `worktree-branch-identity`. The dependency chain is: feature-lock primitive (US-001) → run lifecycle holds both locks (US-002) → project identity by remote (US-004 — must not land before the locks that make it safe) → tooling sees both locks (US-003) → run attribution (US-005) → curator fail-closed (US-006). Test files in `test/unit/{errors,execution/helpers,utils/utils-helpers,precheck/precheck-checks-tier1-blockers,commands/unlock}.test.ts` must be updated alongside the ACs they assert.

### Architecture decisions
- Non-blocking try-locks (never wait) on both sides — no wait cycle possible between them.
- Two predicates kept distinct: `isLockReclaimable` (acquire semantics) and `isLockSuspect` (precheck semantics). They diverge for `host == this machine && pid alive` (reclaimable, not suspect) versus age-based fallbacks (only suspect at 2h). Collapsing them would flip a verdict.
- Host comparison is case-insensitive to tolerate Windows/macOS hostname casing differences.
- Single `buildRunId(workdir, now)` producer with a workdir hash (basename would collide for `git worktree add ../repo-feat`). Output is path-separator-free for safe filename interpolation.
- `isSameProject` is a pure comparator over two remotes (not identity records), so the normalization is reusable from both `claimProjectIdentity` and `checkInitCollision`.
- Refusals carry holder data so error messages don't have to re-read the lock file (a TOCTOU race).
outOfScope: Feature-scoped story worktree branch naming is delivered by the `worktree-branch-identity` feature, which must merge before this one.
Running the same feature concurrently from two checkouts stays refused; the feature lock exists to refuse it.
Running two different features concurrently from the same checkout stays refused by the checkout lock.
Retiring or removing `<workdir>/nax.lock`, and removing the `nax.lock` entry from `.gitignore`, are not part of this feature.
Repositories whose `origin` remotes differ after normalization, including forks, still produce `RUN_NAME_COLLISION`; merging distinct remotes into one project is not delivered.
`<outputDir>/status.json` stays last-writer-wins across concurrent different-feature runs; a per-feature project-level status file is not delivered.
Readers of feature-scoped state under `<outputDir>/features/<feature>/` are not audited, because the feature lock serializes every writer of that subtree.

The project-level directories `cost/`, `usage/`, `prompt-audit/`, `tool-audit/`, `finish-audit/`, `cycle-shadow/` and `mcp/` were not audited for concurrency safety; only the readers listed in the Design's read-surface table were examined.
The `nax plan` precheck path keeps checkout-only stale-lock checking; threading a feature lock through it is not part of this feature.
Changing `nax migrate --reclaim` or `--merge` semantics is not part of this feature.
Reclaiming a lock held on another host by any signal other than age is not delivered; there is no cross-host liveness channel.
Rewriting run IDs already recorded in the old format is not part of this feature; only newly generated run IDs carry the workdir component.
